name: BridgeMind
subcategory: AI tutoring and tech skills courses
tagline: AI-assisted learning platform for tech skills: guided courses, practice exercises, and a chatbot tutor.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The machinery here is not hard: a syllabus generator, lesson rendering, quizzes, a progress table, and an LLM that answers questions with the current lesson stuffed into context. An agent can build that in a session and it will work for one motivated learner. What it will not produce is a curriculum someone actually sequenced and tested, exercises with real graders, or the mild social pressure of a product you paid for. Self-generated lessons also drift: the model happily invents a plausible-sounding module order and you have no way to know it is wrong until you are three weeks in. Build it if you want a study harness you control, not if you want someone else's judgment about what to learn next.
coreLoopDIY: Generate a syllabus for a topic, walk lesson by lesson with an LLM tutor in context, take auto-graded quizzes, and track what you have finished and what needs review.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Willingness to accept model-generated curriculum with no expert review
Local Python runtime or Pyodide if you want runnable code exercises
whatYouLose: A curriculum a human sequenced and revised, instead of one a model improvised on first ask
Hands-on labs with real environments and graded output
Certification-aligned content that tracks exam blueprints as they change
Any external accountability, streaks that mean something, or a completion record anyone else recognizes
moatNotes: The defensible part is authored and maintained course content plus graded labs, not the chat layer bolted onto it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because deciding what to learn, in what order, is the actual hard part, and paying someone for that decision is cheaper than getting it wrong. A model will generate a syllabus for anything you ask, confidently, and you will not be able to evaluate it until you have wasted the time. Maintained course content also stays current with tooling and exam changes, which your one-shot build does not. And a paid subscription is a commitment device: a folder on your laptop is not.
notes: Build the study harness, borrow the syllabus from somewhere human-written, and you get most of the value for the price of an API key.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user study app called "Tutor" for learning technical topics with an LLM.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the UI
- Express (TypeScript) API on port 8787
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/tutor.db
- Anthropic or OpenAI SDK, key read from .env as LLM_API_KEY and LLM_PROVIDER
- No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no hosted services. It runs on localhost only.

Data model (SQLite):
- courses: id, title, topic, level, created_at
- modules: id, course_id, position, title, summary
- lessons: id, module_id, position, title, body_markdown, status (new | in_progress | done)
- quiz_items: id, lesson_id, question, choices_json, answer_index, explanation
- reviews: id, lesson_id, due_on, ease (SM-2 lite: again / hard / good / easy)
- messages: id, lesson_id, role, content, created_at

Features, in scope:
1. "New course" form: topic, target level, hours per week. Call the LLM once to produce a JSON syllabus of modules and lesson titles. Validate the JSON with zod, reject and retry once on failure, show the raw response on second failure.
2. Lesson view: generate the lesson body as markdown on first open, cache it in SQLite, never regenerate unless the user clicks "regenerate".
3. Tutor chat panel on each lesson. Send the lesson body plus the last 10 messages as context. Stream tokens to the UI.
4. "Quiz me" button: generate 5 multiple-choice items for the lesson, store them, grade client-side, show explanations.
5. Spaced review: after a quiz, schedule the lesson with a simple SM-2 lite interval. A "Due today" page lists lessons to revisit.
6. Progress page: percent complete per course, quiz accuracy over time, current review backlog.
7. "Import syllabus" textarea that accepts a pasted markdown outline and builds a course from it, bypassing generation.

Out of scope, do not build:
video, code execution sandboxes, certificates, multi-user, mobile app, payments, cloud sync.

Requirements:
- One command dev setup: npm install then npm run dev starts both server and client (use concurrently).
- Every LLM call logged to ./data/llm.log with prompt, model, and token counts so cost is visible.
- Seed script that creates one example course offline from a hardcoded outline so the app is usable before any API key is set.
- README with setup, .env.example, and a blunt paragraph noting that generated syllabi are unreviewed and should be sanity-checked against a real curriculum.
